title: Haunted road trip through eastern Nebraska, western Iowa
excerpt: Spooky season is here, and what better way to celebrate than visiting some of the most haunted places in Nebraska and Iowa?
content:
KETV's haunted road trip through eastern Nebraska, western Iowa

Related coverage in video above: Famous ghost hunters investigate Omaha home allegedly haunted by Civil War veteran

Spooky season is here, and what better way to celebrate than visiting some of the most haunted places in Nebraska and Iowa?

KETV NewsWatch 7 has put together the most thrilling list, perfect for a spine-tingling road trip, of some of the most haunted places in eastern Nebraska and western Iowa.

Antelope Park

Located in Lincoln, the park is said to be haunted by a woman named Nancy. Witnesses have reported seeing an apparition of a woman in a white, flowy dress wandering the area. Others have reported seeing an apparition going across the field behind the caretaker's house and into the woods.

Argo Hotel

Located in Crofton, the bed and breakfast is said to be haunted by a young girl who died in the basement. The hotel was featured on the TV show Ghost Hunters. There have been reports of doors opening and things moving on their own.

Bailey House Museum

Located in Brownville, Nebraska, it is the house of Civil War Captain Bailey. He was allegedly poisoned by a neighbor, and his spirit still haunts the residence. Those who work at the museum have reported doors that will not remain closed and hearing piano music at night.

Barnard Park

Located near E Military Avenue and N Irving Street in Fremont, the park is said to have once been home to a cemetery, and not all of the bodies were removed by accident. It's said their spirits roam the area, including reports of seeing a woman crying.

Black Angel

Located near N 6th Street and Military Avenue in Council Bluffs, Ruth Anne Dodge's memorial now takes on the name the "Black Angel." It's said she was visited by an angel in her dreams multiple times before her death, which then sparked the legend that if the Black Angel visits you, you will die. Another legend is that if you look in the statue's eyes, you will meet your demise.

Blackbird Hill

Located near Decatur, Nebraska, it is the site of Omaha Indian Chief Blackbird's grave, but it's said that it's not his spirit that haunts this area. The spirit of a woman who allegedly murdered her husband. And it is said her screams can be heard every Oct. 17, the anniversary of her death.

Brother Sebastian's Steakhouse

It's rumored that a regular customer who died visits the establishment, relighting candles and opening doors.

Calvary Cemetery

Located in Sioux City, Iowa, the cemetery is the second oldest in the town. Witnesses have reported ringing in their ears and the sensation of cobwebs on their faces. The sensations are said to get stronger the closer people get to a grave carved from a tree. Legend has it that the tree was used for hangings.

Captain Meriwether Lewis Dredge

Located in Brownville, the now-museum is thought to be haunted, and guests have reported hearing the piano play while no one is around.

Clarkson Historic Opera House

Located in Clarkson, visitors have reported hearing ghostly laughter and seeing apparitions wandering the halls.

Columbus Hy-Vee

Located in Columbus at 3010 23rd St., the grocery store is said to be haunted by a ghost named Scooter. Witnesses claim Scooter makes screeching sounds around the produce and dairy sections in the middle of the night.

Cornerstone Mansion Bed and Breakfast

Located just off of 39th and Dodge streets in Omaha, the bed and breakfast dates back to the 1800s, and guests who have stayed there have reported seeing apparitions and spirits roaming the halls.

Doane University Library

Located in Crete, the library is said to be haunted by a woman in a white dress, who can be seen in the front windows.

Earling Exorcism

In 1928, the Franciscan convent, located at 207 2nd St., was the scene of a 23-day exorcism that has been the story of multiple Hollywood movies, including the 2025 Al Pacino film "The Ritual." It is said that during the exorcism of Emma Schmidt, she flew across the room, clinging to the wall above the door. Schmidt was said to have lived a normal life after the incident. Witnesses claimed to hear weird noises and smell bad odors coming from the building.

Forest Lawn Cemetery Chapel

Located near N 54th Street and Mormon Bridge Road in Omaha, the cemetery's chapel is said to be home to a shadowy mass that roams the basement. Some people have noted feeling ill or feeling electricity pulsing through them while inside the chapel.

Fort Omaha

Located at 30th and Fort streets, the north Omaha part of the Metropolitan Community College campus was once a military post and has been reported as haunted, with visitors reporting having seen ghosts in several of the buildings.

Ghost Bridge of Logan Creek

Located in Pender, the legend has it that in the early 1900s, a train was held up by men who were chasing down a man who allegedly murdered a family. The men hanged him from the bridge as the train passed over it. Some have said a dark smudge can be seen while looking at the landscape, where he was allegedly hanged.

The Granary

Located in the area of 75th and Main streets in Ralston, numerous guests have claimed the premises are haunted.

Hatchet House

Located near E 3rd and N Jefferson streets in Papillion, the one-room schoolhouse has an eerie legend behind it. It's said a schoolteacher beheaded all of her students in the early 1900s. It's also said she took out their hearts and dumped them in a nearby creek. Visitors who find the Heartbeat Bridge report hearing the heartbeats of the children, plus other weird occurrences.

Historic Klondike Hotel

Located in Manilla, Iowa, the Victorian-era hotel is said to be haunted by a former resident. Witnesses have reported seeing the rocking chair move on its own. Others have reported the feeling of needing to get out of the chair.

Hummel Park

Located near John J Pershing Drive and Ponca Road in Omaha, the park has multiple urban legends that surround its history. It's said to be where satanic ritual murders have taken place. Graffiti has helped keep that legend alive. Some say the spirits of those who were lynched in the park still roam the area. Another popular urban legend is that a family or group of albino people living in the park. All the legends are what give this Omaha park its reputation for everything spooky.

James F. Lynch Park

Located near 24th and Martha streets in Omaha, the park is said to be haunted by a man. Visitors have reported seeing the man crying for help during the night. Others have reported hearing footsteps and a baby crying.

Jewell Park

Located near Combs Road and Washington Street in Bellevue, visitors have reported hearing disembodied voices and footsteps. Others have said to have heard disembodied sounds of farm animals.

Joslyn Castle

Located at 39th and Davenport streets in Omaha, the four-story, 35-room mansion is said to be haunted by the homeowners and their adopted daughter. Multiple paranormal investigations have occurred on the castle's grounds. There have been spectral voices heard by employees, sightings of a woman in a white dress on the main staircase, and a voice yelling "get out" among a series of other odd events.

Malvern Manor

Located in Malvern, Iowa, the building has a rich history. It was built during the 1800s during the railroad era, and it served traveler and railroad workers, who were passing by. Then it became a place for community gatherings as it transitioned into "The Cottage Hotel" before it was transformed into a care facility for those with mental illness and developmental disabilities in the early-to-mid 1900s. Eventually, the building was abandoned for years. In the 2010s Malvern Manor gained national attention after being featured on a paranormal program. As of now, it's paranormal reputation is known throughout the world with guests reporting hearing disembodied screams, feeling someone breathing in their ears, and seeing shadow figures roaming the hallways.

Morgan Hall

Located on Peru State College's campus, the girls' dormitory is said to be haunted by a woman named Eliza C. Morgan, who allegedly died in the basement. Residents have reported faucets turning off and on, strange noises, and voices.

Museum of the Shadows

Located in Omaha at 1110 Douglas St., the museum is considered "one of the most haunted museums in the world!" Home to more than 5,000 "verified" haunted artifacts, it's been featured on the Travel Channel, Discovery+ and Prime Video. Go on a self-guided tour, meet museum curator Nate Raterman or attempt the sit challenge — 10 minutes alone in complete darkness, surrounded by haunted objects with only a flashlight if you need to tap out.

Nebraska State Capitol

Located near 14th and K streets in Lincoln, the building is said to be haunted, with several witnesses reporting an apparition that appeared to be falling. Others have said they saw an apparition screaming or crying.

Prospect Hill Cemetery

Located at 32nd and Parker streets in Omaha, the cemetery is considered the most haunted cemetery in the state. It is the final resting place for about 15,000 of the first Nebraskan settlers. Notable Civil War veterans, criminals, and wealthy people lie here. It has unusual tombstones, including the tombstone of an infamous madame, Anna Wilson, and her partner, Dan Allen, whose spirits are said to roam the area. It is also thought to be the site of a Native American burial ground, which only adds to the lore. Starting in the mid-late 1800s, a ghost story of the Woman in White that mysteriously roams throughout the property began, and there have been many sightings since. Shadowy figures have been reported to follow visitors around, even cornering them inside the mausoleum.

Robber's Cave

Located in southwest Lincoln, it's said to have once been a place for the Pawnee Native Americans to contact their god Tirawa. Other legends claimed it was a stop on the Underground Railroad and a hideout for Jesse James, among others. Witnesses have claimed to have heard Native American chants as well as screaming, crying and laughter.

Shell Creek

Located near Platte Center, legend has it that three men were buried alive in the creek bed in the early 1900s when a cave they had dug collapsed. Witnesses claim to have seen three apparitions at night digging.

Seven Sisters Road

Located near Nebraska City, the road is also known as Road L on an official map. An old tale of a father who was angry and hanged his seven daughters on separate hills surrounds the stretch of road. Visitors have reported experiencing car malfunctions, car batteries draining, and hearing women screaming.

Sioux City Municipal Auditorium

Located in Sioux City, an electrician was allegedly electrocuted during the building of the auditorium. He is believed to haunt the building, flicking lights on and off. Witnesses have reported feeling a cold spot near where he died.

Squirrel Cage Jail

Located near S 6th and Pearl streets in Council Bluffs, the former rotary jail-turned-museum is one of three in the U.S., and it is the biggest of the three. There have been reports of cabinets and doors slamming, a little girl's voice, and ghost cats. It's said the fourth floor has the greatest number of reported sightings.

St. Mary's Cemetery

Located in Hamburg, Iowa, the cemetery is said to be haunted by a woman. Witnesses claimed the woman could be seen kneeling at the feet of the statue of the Virgin Mary. Others have said wailing sounds are coming from the statues.

Temple Building

Located near 12th and R streets in Lincoln on the University of Nebraska's campus, the building is home to the theatre department. It is rumored to have three spirits haunting the facility. The first is of a worker who died during the construction of the building. The second is of a former director in the theater department, who has been reportedly seen in the balcony during rehearsals and performances. The third spirit is of a former student who allegedly died during a production of Macbeth.

Villisca Ax Murder House

Located in Villisca, Iowa, two adults and six children were brutally murdered in 1912. The murders were never solved. Visitors have reported hearing children's voices, communicating with the dead, and feeling cold spots throughout the house.

White House Apartments

Located near 10th and William streets in Omaha, it was built as a hospital and then later turned into apartments. Residents have reported seeing an apparition of a woman in a white gown in the lobby and hallways.

Wildwood Historic Center

Located near 4th Corso and Steinhart Road in Nebraska City, the historic home is rumored to be haunted after visitors have reported seeing a lady in a long black dress in the kitchen. Others have heard children's voices upstairs.

Witch's Grave

Located in Aurora, the cemetery is home to the legend of a supposed witch who is buried there. Rumors say the woman was hanged for being odd, and others claim the woman was completely normal. Iron poles connected by chains were placed around the grave, and it's said that the chains have been found mysteriously broken multiple times.
